keyVerseText: And Ozias begat Joatham; and Joatham begat Achaz; and Achaz begat Ezekias;
rootMeaning: The name Ἀχάζ (Acház) originates from the Hebrew אָחָז (ʼÂchâz), which means "he has grasped." This root sense implies a strong act of holding or seizing, suggesting one who takes hold firmly. Beyond the English transliteration, the original Hebrew conveys a sense of possession or control, which enriches the understanding of the name as more than a mere label, but as an expression of character or destiny.
usageInScripture: The word Ἀχάζ appears twice in the New Testament, both times transliterated as 'Achaz,' maintaining consistency in its translation. It specifically refers to an Israelite figure, notably a king of Judah and ancestor in the Messianic genealogy. This consistent use highlights the importance of the name as identifying a historical and theological link in the lineage of Christ, emphasizing its rootedness in Israelite history and covenantal promise.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Acház as "he has grasped" deepens the theological appreciation of God's providential hand in history, especially in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. The name points to God's sovereign grasp over His people and His unfolding plan of redemption through their lineage. Recognizing Acház as a historical figure in the Messiah's ancestry underscores God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promises despite human frailty. This connection invites believers to trust in God's control and purpose, even in complex or challenging circumstances.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 1:9 states, 'And Ozias begat Joatham; and Joatham begat Achaz; and Achaz begat Ezekias,' situating Acház firmly within the royal lineage leading to Christ. The presence of Acház here is more than genealogical—it marks a pivotal link in God's redemptive plan. The name's meaning, 'he has grasped,' resonates with the idea of God holding fast to His covenant through successive generations, culminating in the birth of Jesus. This verse invites reflection on the continuity of God's promises and the assurance that He holds history in His hands.
